get.description:
This agent's OAuth client, as a document (CIMD).

An authorization server that supports Client ID Metadata
Documents accepts a **URL** as the `client_id` and fetches that
URL to learn who the client is. No registration step, no issued
secret, nothing to go stale.

This is how a client gets into a provider that publishes no
`registration_endpoint` — Sumologic and ServiceNow both advertise
`client_id_metadata_document_supported`, which is why an MCP
client can reach them from a bare URL while dynamic registration
is impossible.

Deliberately unauthenticated: the authorization server fetches it
server-to-server, with no credentials, before any user is
involved. It contains nothing secret — it is the public
description of this client.

agent is going to reply — the difference between a channel
people trust and one they stop using.

Answer the pending action — only if the run is yours (E33-T4).

Being in the space is what lets somebody *see* this. Answering
it is bound to the person who started the run, because the
agent will act with their access and not the approver's.

The room, from `after_seq` onwards, oldest first (E33-T2).

`after_seq` is how a reconnect resumes: the client hands back the
last sequence it saw and gets exactly what it missed. Order is the
database's sequence, not a clock, so two readers and one reader
twice see the same order.

get.description:
Who `@` may address in this room (E41-T3).

Assembled per request from the directory and from the timeline,
never from a stored roster. The directory half is read for
display only — posting here is gated on membership by the
timeline, which asks the directory itself, so this list grants
nothing.

The timeline half is what makes the picker work when the
directory cannot answer, and it is the strictest reading of
"offer only what this person can already see": those names are
on their screen.
What the room has bookmarked, newest pin first.

Who is mid-run here, so the room can show it (E31-T4).

Presence is the point: two people independently approving the
same tool call is a double write nobody intended, and the
first defence is seeing that somebody else is already acting.

get.description:
What this room cost this month, and who spent it.

Both halves, because either alone is unusable: a room total
with nobody behind it cannot be acted on, and a person's total
says nothing about which room to look at.

The total is the sum of the rows rather than a stored figure, so
the two cannot drift apart. The rate card version travels with
it — a number with no version beside it cannot be checked
against the contract that priced it.

The room, pushed rather than polled (E33-T2).

Same contract as `GET /messages`: everything after a sequence
the client already holds. A stream and a poll want exactly the
same thing, so reconnecting after a dropped connection is the
ordinary case rather than a recovery path.

**Membership is re-asked on every tick, not at connect.** An
open stream is a standing read, and a member removed from the
directory group must stop receiving the room — within a tick,
not whenever they next reload. SEC-3 holds here because the
check lives in `timeline.read`, which this calls in a loop.

decorator or security scheme can run first -- an unauthenticated caller
would get their body spooled to temp disk before being told 404 or 401.
